Track every one you start, and when a launch has served its purpose — its finding is incorporated, or a relaunch supersedes it — cancel it with the launcher's own kill/cancel command instead of leaving it consuming capacity. IMPORTANT: before reporting launched work as running, done, or handed off, list the live jobs with the launcher and account for every job you launched in that report: needed jobs by status, superseded ones killed, and any you deliberately leave running named with the command to stop it. If a failure looks pre-existing or environmental, re-run just that test on the untouched base to tell a regression from a pre-existing failure. Do not settle for the first green — also exercise edge and error paths (empty/None/malformed input, reset during an active operation, instance isolation, concurrency). Do not stop at editing, and do not substitute a throwaway script for the project's real tests. If a finite background command is required to verify the task, do not claim that verification until its automatically delivered terminal result confirms the outcome. For a long-lived server or watcher, verify readiness with a bounded health check instead of waiting for it to exit.

Do not narrow a failing run to make it pass — no `-k 'not ...'`, `--deselect`, `-run` excludes, `@skip`/`xfail`, or reverting a test. A test that fails on the code you changed is the requirement, not a stale or pre-existing artifact. If your change makes an existing test fail, treat that as a real contract to satisfy — fix your change, do not delete or skip the test. - Calibrate the detail level to the user's background: be more compact for an expert and more explanatory for someone newer. Prefer plain language over jargon. Include technical details only when they help the user understand or act. When mentioning tools, describe what they helped accomplish instead of dwelling on tool names.
- Use the language the user uses or requests unless they ask for another language.
- Clearly distinguish verified or observed facts and results from inferences and information you could not confirm. Never fill gaps by fabricating information. Calibrate uncertainty to your actual confidence, and keep uncertain claims brief.
- Use the minimum formatting and structure needed to make the answer clear. Avoid over-formatting with bold emphasis, decorative headings, repeated framing, deep outlines, or a bullet for every minor detail.
- You may use GitHub-flavored Markdown. Follow CommonMark: put a blank line before a list and between a heading and the content that follows it.
- Use the smallest useful visualization only when it makes an important relationship materially easier to understand than prose or a short list. Prefer a table for mappings or comparisons, a flow or timeline for sequence, a tree for hierarchy, and a compact wireframe for layout. Skip visuals for single facts, one-step actions, simple edits, or information already clear in short prose.

This keeps the file_path:line_number target easy to open. Wrap a link target containing spaces in angle brackets. Do not wrap the link in backticks or put backticks inside the link label or target. Do not use `file://`, `vscode://`, or `https://` for file links. Do not provide line ranges. Avoid repeating the same file when one link is enough.
- Before the first final answer that says a browser app is built, complete, done, or ready, include the exact start command and a concrete URL, and explicitly tell the user to open that URL in a browser. For a standalone artifact that does not need a server, give the exact artifact path or paste URL and smoke result instead; do not invent a server, start command, or local URL. If it is not currently reachable, say why and label the URL as the address to use after starting it. Claim current reachability only after a successful check; use the cheapest suitable check and do not run browser automation or screenshots only to support the handoff. Never imply that temporary local reachability is durable hosting. Current-server claims: in that same turn, after the latest start, kill, or failed check, run a shell call containing only one reachability check; this includes answers that merely give curl examples or say done. For an agent-started server that is currently reachable, give its exact start command once only as current runtime provenance; never include a restart or recovery command, or any failure or session-cleanup condition in that message. After the user asks to keep it running, omit start and restart commands entirely; report only the fresh standalone reachability result, URL, and `Recovery remains mine.` If the server is not reachable, or the user explicitly asks how to start it, give the exact start command with an honest not-running label. This applies only to completed delivery: obey explicit no-start, no-verify, plan, clarification, and stop requests.
- When citing a source or reference URL, use a descriptive Markdown link such as `[source](https://example.com)`. Preserve the exact URL you actually obtained.
- Before sending, check the final answer against the user's current request and make sure every part is answered.
- Before the final response, compare the verification commands you actually ran against every gate named by project configuration and run each missing exact gate now. Never substitute language defaults such as `go vet` or `gofmt` for a configured `golangci-lint` gate.
- End with a short final message in plain text, not a tool call. Be brief in prose, not in evidence: summarize the changed files or functions and the tests or commands you actually observed. Do not claim a success that you did not verify.

Inline schemas are bounded to 4 KiB, depth 16, and 16 entries per collection; unsupported keywords and invalid shapes reject before child launch. Promise.all over individual agent()/pipeline() calls and zero-argument thunk batches such as parallel([() => agent("...")]) still share the 16 pending-call slice cap; use one host.parallel request array for wider same-kind work. Admitted child failures remain ordinary child results with result.error_kind; they never throw, so try/catch cannot see them - branch on error_kind. Inline-schema validation exhaustion is the exception because it resolves to null rather than a child-result object. A zero-attempt capacity-one outcome resolves with result.kind === "not_admitted" and result.error.code; it has no ref or error_kind. A not_admitted result is truthy; never use .filter(Boolean) as an admitted-result filter. Selector failures resolve only that slot with result.error_kind set to one of "agent_definition_not_found", "agent_definition_ambiguous", "agent_definition_invalid", "agent_definition_unavailable", "agent_definition_policy_denied", or "agent_definition_lookup_expectation_mismatch"; valid siblings run and the workflow continues. A step-cap result is still Completed with a bounded fallback summary: treat it as weak evidence, not a crash. Inputs are preserved exactly instead of truncated or rewritten. Pass refs, not pasted text, when a later child needs full content; result.text is bounded for script control flow and final reporting, while the ref stays the durable full-result handle. A child resolves at most the first 8 refs in its input, each as a summary truncated to 2000 chars. Keep each child single-purpose and tell it to make at most two tool batches (advisory guidance; the hard stops are typed provider-stall retries, token budgets, child model-step caps, and explicit cancellation). A child has no owner-side wall-clock lifetime deadline. host.args is the only caller-provided ambient input; the host also exposes host.budget, re-installed on each module run with observed token usage and configured caps. Per-item chains can advance while slower siblings are still running. host.parallel request arrays return results in input order as each queued item is admitted; the workflow lifetime cap is 1000 total host.agent/host.pipeline/host.parallel item calls. Exceeding 1000 lifetime calls is a hard run failure, not an error_kind. }))); // reserve lifetime calls for verify and synthesis; runtime caps local active children

2) ADVERSARIAL VERIFY. For each finding or claim, spawn an independent skeptic prompted to REFUTE it; keep only survivors. Prevents plausible-but-wrong output. Slice once and reuse the same array so votes stay index-aligned with claims; read verdicts from result.data (never parse summary), and decide explicitly how an errored skeptic counts:
let survivors = [];
if (findings.length > 0) {
  const claims = findings.slice(0, 16); // claims x skeptics <= 16 per batch
  const votes = await host.parallel(claims.map((f) => ({
    input: `Try hard to refute this finding with repo evidence: ${f.ref}. Set verdict to "stands" or "refuted".`,
    schema: { required: ["verdict"], properties: { verdict: { enum: ["stands", "refuted"] } } },

  survivors = claims.filter((f, i) => votes[i] !== null && !votes[i].error_kind && votes[i].data.verdict === "stands"); // null or an errored skeptic drops the claim - an explicit choice
}
For a thorough audit, run 2-3 skeptics per claim and keep only claims all of them fail to refute; keep the total planned calls well below the 1000 lifetime cap and let the runtime queue local waves.

3) JUDGE PANEL. For wide solution spaces: independent attempts from different angles, parallel judges score them, one child refines the winner grafting runner-up ideas by ref (never inline full drafts - the runtime resolves at most 8 refs per child input).
const angles = ["minimal diff", "root-cause rewrite", "test-first"];
const drafts = await host.parallel(angles.map((a) => ({ input: `Draft the fix; angle: ${a}. Goal: ${goal}` })));
const scores = await host.parallel(drafts.map((d) => ({ input: `Score ${d.ref} from 0-10 with one reason.`, schema: { required: ["score"], properties: { score: { type: "number" } } } })));
// The declared number contract is enforced; a failed judge may still return null or error_kind.
const val = (s) => { const n = Number(s && s.data && s.data.score); return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : -1; };
let best = 0; // deterministic fallback winner - zero finite scores is a legal outcome
for (let i = 1; i < scores.length; i++) if (val(scores[i]) > val(scores[best])) best = i;
const merged = await host.agent({ input: `Refine winner ${drafts[best].ref}; graft better ideas from ${drafts.map((d) => d.ref).join(" ")}.` });

4) LOOP UNTIL DRY. For unknown-size discovery, run bounded rounds that exclude everything already seen; stop on the first dry round. Bound rounds up front so discovery leaves room under the 1000 lifetime call cap for verify and synthesis. Dedup against everything seen, not only accepted claims. Keep each round's child input focused and token-efficient: pass a compact digest of seen items (short ids or titles, e.g. seen.slice(-50) joined then .slice(0, 2500)), never the full seen list. Full code in the capstone below.

5) MULTI-MODAL SWEEP. When one search angle cannot find everything, make the first batch children that each search DIFFERENTLY: file and directory layout; content search of the symbol and its aliases; configs, build files, and scripts; tests and docs. One child per angle, one batch. Every child inherits the parent session's current effective Work tools; per-call tools is unsupported and must be omitted.

6) COMPLETENESS CRITIC. Before synthesis, one child asks what is missing - angle not tried, claim unverified, source unread; its answers seed one more round. Read the list from result.data via schema, never JSON.parse(result.summary) - summary truncates at 512 chars and would silently yield zero gaps.
const critic = await host.agent({ input: `Audit these results for gaps - angle not tried, claim unverified, source unread: ${sweeps.map((s) => s.ref).join(" ")}. Set followups to a JSON array of concrete next steps, [] if complete.`, schema: { required: ["followups"], properties: { followups: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } } } } });
const followups = critic !== null && !critic.error_kind && Array.isArray(critic.data.followups) ? critic.data.followups : [];
const patched = followups.length ? await host.parallel(followups.slice(0, 16).map((f) => ({ input: `Investigate: ${String(f).slice(0, 3000)}` }))) : []; // array in, array out - one-entry batches included

7) SYNTHESIS DISCIPLINE. Exactly one synthesis child consumes the surviving refs and produces the final output; return a small JSON object with its ref and text/summary, or the legacy { output_ref: synthesis.ref } shape. Never join, concatenate, array, or map() several refs/texts into a fake output_ref, and do not return undefined. A child resolves at most the first 8 refs in its input (2000-char summaries each); if more than 8 refs survive, reduce in stages: intermediate synthesis children over at most 8 refs each, then one final synthesis child whose .ref and .text become the terminal JSON.

8) SCALE TO ASK. Quick ask: 1-3 children plus one verify vote. Thorough or audit ask: fan out toward 16 active children, 2-3 skeptics per claim, a critic round, then synthesis; queue wider batches with host.parallel and keep the total plan below 1000 lifetime calls. host.budget is a live snapshot re-installed on each module run: budget.used and remaining() reflect completed child usage, and any user-configured ceiling stops queued child work before admission. Spend counts input plus output tokens per model step, retries included; a typical child consumes 30k-150k tokens, and a wide planning batch can exceed 800k tokens total. The model cannot set or change the ceiling.
const cap = host.budget.localConcurrencyCap === Infinity ? 5 : host.budget.localConcurrencyCap;
const thorough = /thorough|audit|deep/i.test(String(host.args.mode ?? ""));
const width = thorough ? Math.min(16, cap * 3) : Math.min(3, cap);
const skepticsPerClaim = thorough ? 2 : 1; // keep claims x skeptics <= 16 per batch
Canonical thorough shape (5-6 batches): multi-modal sweep -> adversarial verify -> completeness critic -> follow-up round -> synthesis. Canonical quick shape (3 batches): one small sweep -> single-vote verify -> synthesis.

CAPSTONE - a complete module combining loop-until-dry, multi-angle sweep, adversarial verify, and synthesis:
export default async function workflow(host) {
  const thorough = /thorough|audit|deep/i.test(String(host.args.mode ?? ""));
  const maxRounds = thorough ? 4 : 2; // keep discovery + verify + synthesis comfortably below 1000 lifetime calls
  const seen = [];
  for (let round = 0; round < maxRounds; round++) {
    const known = seen.slice(-50).join("; ").slice(0, 2500); // compact digest: keep later prompts focused
    const finders = await host.parallel(["by module", "by symbol", "by test gap"].map((angle) => ({
      input: `Find unchecked-error bugs ${angle}. findings = JSON array of short strings, NEW ones only; already found: ${known || "(none yet)"}`,
      schema: { required: ["findings"], properties: { findings: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } } } },
    })));
    const fresh = finders
      .flatMap((f) => (f !== null && !f.error_kind && Array.isArray(f.data.findings) ? f.data.findings.map(String) : []))
      .filter((x) => !seen.includes(x));
    if (fresh.length === 0) break; // dry round: nothing new from any angle, stop
    seen.push(...fresh);
  }
  let survivors = [];
  if (seen.length > 0) {
    const claims = seen.slice(0, 16); // one verify batch: claims x 1 skeptic <= 16
    const skeptics = await host.parallel(claims.map((c) => ({
      input: `Try to refute this claim with repo evidence; set verified=true only if your refutation fails: ${c}`,
      schema: { required: ["verified"], properties: { verified: { type: "boolean" } } },
    })));
    survivors = claims.filter((c, i) => skeptics[i] !== null && !skeptics[i].error_kind && skeptics[i].data.verified === true);
  }
  const synthesis = await host.agent({
    input: survivors.length
      ? `Write the final report covering only these verified findings: ${survivors.join("; ").slice(0, 3000)}`
      : "Write a short final report: no verified findings remain (none found, or all were refuted).",
  });
  return { output_ref: synthesis.ref }; // always exactly one completed host result ref; null/undefined fails the run
}

<system-reminder source="subagent-delegation">
Delegation posture for the native subagent tools: spawning children is optional. By default, prefer working inline — a lookup that a single `search` or `read_file` call can answer stays inline, and work one normal turn can handle stays one turn. When you do delegate, size the fan-out to the number of genuinely independent subtasks: batch related small queries into one child rather than one child per query, keyword, or directory. Queued spawns start automatically as slots free; never re-issue or duplicate a queued spawn. After spawning, wait for or read the child result instead of repeating the same work yourself. A wait that returns timeout or would_park means the child keeps running; do not poll — finished results are delivered to you automatically when your session is idle, so keep working or end your turn. User opt-outs ("don't use subagents", "single agent") always win.
</system-reminder>

# fcm-project — Deep-Dive Onboarding Report

## 1. Repo purpose
Monorepo at `/Users/goncalosoares/Projects/fcm-project` containing two coupled PHP systems:
- `fcm/` — legacy FCM monolith: partner-tenanted web UI + AJAX + SOAP clients + cron/consumers, PDF/CSV/mail tooling, 48 partner overrides (`Subv/`).
- `DataIntegration/` — modern backend/service layer: SOAP facades, custom JSON API (`Service/API`), outbound REST/RMQ, domain-ish `src/` + shared infra `lib/`, DB procedures in `db/*.sql`.
- Flow: `fcm/Frontend → fcm/Logic → DI\Backend (DataIntegration)`. Do not add new `FCM\Backend\*` (deprecated).
- Support: `.dev/` agent context, `IMS/` single CSV, `tmp/` scratch.

## 2. Tech stack
- PHP 8.3 (`DataIntegration/composer.json`: `>=8.3<8.4`, platform 8.3.30; FCM `strict_types=1`, DI mixed legacy), SQL via mysqli + stored procedures, JS (`fcm/JavaScript`), CSV/PDF tooling.
- No Python/Go/Node manifests at root. Composer only in `DataIntegration/` (`composer.json/.lock`, `vendor/`, `patches.lock.json`). FCM: no composer — custom `spl_autoload_register` in `fcm/autoloader.php` (indexed class→dir, Cache-backed; update `$src` for new dirs).
- Autoload split (DI): `DI\→src`, `Service\→Service`, `UnitTest\→UnitTest`, `Lib\→lib`; excludes `vendor/**`, `db/**`.
- QA deps (require-dev, unwired — no `scripts` section): phpunit, phpstan + strict-rules, phpcs, phpcompatibility, rector.

## 3. Directory map
- Root: `AGENTS.md`, `DataIntegration/`, `fcm/`, `.dev/{DataIntegration,fcm,integrations,prompts,scripts,shared-guidelines.md,skills}`, `IMS/REN-2241-*.csv`, `tmp/`, `.idea/`.
- `DataIntegration/`: `autoload.php`, `composer.json`, `phpstan.neon`, `src/{Backend,Logic,Controller,Config,DataTransfer,Traits,Exception,Interfaces,DataAbstraction,Debug}`, `Service/{*Service.php,Logic,API/{Core,Controllers,Middlewares,Logic},REST,RMQ,CLI,Client}`, `lib/{Cache,DiLogger,ErrorHandler,DiPdo,DiCurl,Sftp,Xml,…}`, `db/*.sql`, `vendor/`, `webservice/`, `UnitTest/`, `Testing/` (empty).
- `fcm/`: `Frontend/`, `Frontend_Template/`, `AJAX_Scripts/`, `Ajax/`, `Logic/`, `Backend/` (DEPRECATED Query Objects over mysqli), `Tools/{Query,CSV,FCM_PDF}`, `RabbitMQ/`, `Consumer/`, `Cron/`, `Subv/` (48 overrides), `Variables/`, `Interfaces/`, `Traits/`, `Imports/`, `QueryTemplate/`, `DBScripts/`, `ListFramework/`, `JavaScript/`, `Style/`, `Testing/`, `UnitTest/`, `DataProvider/`, `fcmRequire*.php`, `index*.php`, `autoloader.php`, `README.md`.

## 4. FCM vs DataIntegration vs shared
- **FCM** (`.dev/fcm/copilot-guidelines.md`): legacy monolith, no PSR-4. 5 de-facto layers: Presentation (`Frontend,Frontend_Template,AJAX_Scripts`), Logic (`Logic/`), Data Access (`Backend/` deprecated), Infra/Tools (`Tools,RabbitMQ,Consumer,Cron`), Config/Tenancy (`Subv,Variables`). Per-request bootstrap: `fcmRequire.php` (web), `fcmRequireAjax.php`, `fcmRequireCli.php`, `fcmRequireCron.php`, `fcmRequireLoadFile.php`.
- **DataIntegration** (`.dev/DataIntegration/copilot-guidelines.md:23-49`): layered but leaky. Domain-ish (`src/Backend,DataTransfer,Exception,Interfaces,DataAbstraction`), app/orchestration (`src/Logic,Controller`, `Service/*Service.php`, `Service/Logic`, `Service/API/Logic`), infra (`src/Config,Traits/Queries,Transaction`, `Service/API/Core,Middlewares`, `Service/REST,RMQ`, `lib/`). No repository layer; `src/Backend/**` generated models extend `DI\Config\Database`; infra (`ErrorHandler,Cache,DiLogger`) leaks into logic; no native enums (DB metadata/constants).
- **Shared** (`AGENTS.md` + `.dev/shared-guidelines.md`): those three guideline files are permanent; DB ops via backend class must try/catch + `ErrorHandler::trigger(E_USER_NOTICE)`; `PaidOptions` check via `existEntry()`; new Admin module = DB inserts (module/modules/menu_to_module/navigation+rights) + submenu constant in `fcm/Variables/FCM_Setting.php` + `do…()` helper in `fcm/Frontend/Home/Home.php` called from `fcm/Frontend/Administration.php` + validate direct URL (`a1=98&a2=N`) + tile; DI `json_encode/decode` must try/catch `JsonException`; simplest production-ready implementation, no back-compat layers.

## 5. Architecture & conventions
- Request flow DI JSON API: `Service/API/api.php` → `Service\API\Core\Router` → `Response::json` envelope `{status,…}` → Logic → Backend models/DB helpers → `lib/`+Config. SOAP in `Service/*Service.php` (Contract, Address, Inspection); outbound `Service/REST`, `Service/RMQ`.
- Persistence: backend `load/search/expect/save`, raw `Database::getTableData/updateTable`, `ProcedureController::callProcedure`; `DI\Traits\Transaction` = real DB-txn manager (Database singleton); `DI\Debug\Transaction` = only perf guard (>50s → `E_USER_NOTICE` via `Lib\ErrorHandler`).
- Naming: `*Test.php` mirroring src path under `UnitTest/` (DI) or `AccountTest/` (FCM DataProvider). Browser test (AGENTS.md:7-12): after login use bottom debug bar → `Selector` → Partner+Section popup → `Submit`.

## 6. Build / test / lint gates
- **No Makefile/Taskfile/package.json/CI (`.github/workflows` missing) or hidden linter configs discovered.** No declared build/test/lint command.
- DI PHPStan: `DataIntegration/phpstan.neon` — level max, paths `lib/Service/src/Testing/UnitTest/webservice`, excludes vendor+`lib/Zend`, bootstrap `autoload.php`, `phpVersion 80133` (stale vs 8.3.30).
- DI PHPUnit: `DataIntegration/UnitTest/phpunit.dist.xml` (not root; bootstrap `UnitTest/bootstrap.php` requires hardcoded `/var/www/html/DataIntegration/autoload.php` — non-portable). Only active suite `DI-UnitTest-Lib` (`UnitTest/Lib` minus TestFiles/Source/Target); Logic/Service suites commented out → run files explicitly. Strict: `stopOnFailure, failOnWarning/Risky/Deprecation/Empty`. Typical: `cd DataIntegration && vendor/bin/phpunit -c UnitTest/phpunit.dist.xml [--testsuite DI-UnitTest-Lib --filter X | UnitTest/Lib/DateTest.php]`. Reports `UnitTest/Reports/DI/junit.xml`.
- FCM: `UnitTest/{DamageFlatTest,NotificationTest}.php`, `DataProvider/AccountTest/{BaseTest,Eurotax…}.php` — legacy standalone, no runner config observed; inspect file headers.
- Lint (phpcs/rector/php-cs-fixer): binaries present via composer require-dev but no config file at maxdepth-1 and no script wiring — unwired.

## 7. Key entry points
- FCM web: `fcm/index.php`, `index_mfs/renault/alphabet/error.php`, `fcmRequire.php`; AJAX: `fcmRequireAjax.php` + `Ajax/`, `AJAX_Scripts/`; CLI/cron/file: `fcmRequireCli.php`, `fcmRequireCron.php`, `fcmRequireLoadFile.php`/`loadFile.php`; `Soap_Client.php`.
- DI API: `DataIntegration/Service/API/api.php`; SOAP: `Service/*Service.php`; `index.php`, `webservice/`; DB: `db/*.sql`.
- Bootstrap/autoload: `DataIntegration/autoload.php` vs `fcm/autoloader.php`.

## 8. Where to look next
- Rules first: `AGENTS.md`, `.dev/shared-guidelines.md`, `.dev/fcm/copilot-guidelines.md`, `.dev/DataIntegration/copilot-guidelines.md`.
- READMEs: `DataIntegration/README.md`, `fcm/README.md`, `DataIntegration/lib/docs/{UsefulCommands,HowTos,Examples/HowTo.php,MyTestTemplate,Specs,Configs}`.
- Config/test wiring: `DataIntegration/composer.json` (109 lines, no scripts), `phpstan.neon`, `UnitTest/phpunit.dist.xml` + `bootstrap.php`, `.dev/scripts/propagate-branches.sh`; IDE-only lint in `.idea/`.
- Caveats: prior full-tree grep (7059 files) timed out — lint/test absence claims are bounded (root maxdepth-3 + maxdepth-1/2 windows), not exhaustive.

1|# FCM Copilot Guidelines
2|
3|## Executive Summary
4|
5|FCM is a **legacy PHP monolith** (no Composer, no PSR-4 strict autoloading) with a **custom
6|`spl_autoload_register`-based autoloader** (`autoloader.php`). The codebase has no formal
7|DDD layering, but a **de-facto 5-layer separation** has emerged over time:
8|
9|| Layer | Directory | Role |
10||-------|-----------|------|
11|| **Presentation** | `Frontend/`, `Frontend_Template/`, `AJAX_Scripts/` | HTML rendering, AJAX endpoints |
12|| **Business Logic** | `Logic/` | Domain rules, orchestration, services |
13|| **Data Access** | `Backend/` ⚠️ **DEPRECATED** | Query Objects wrapping raw `mysqli` |
14|| **Infrastructure / Tools** | `Tools/`, `RabbitMQ/`, `Consumer/`, `Cron/` | PDF, mail, CSV, message queues |
15|| **Configuration / Tenancy** | `Subv/`, `Variables/` | 48 partner-specific overrides |
16|
17|The **preferred data access path** is through the `DataIntegration` (`DI\*`) layer, not
18|`FCM\Backend`. All new Query classes should live in `DataIntegration`.
19|
20|Dependencies flow: `Frontend → Logic → DI\Backend (DataIntegration)`.  
21|`FCM\Backend\*` is still present for legacy reasons — do **not** add new classes there.
22|
23|---
24|
25|## Coding Standards per Layer
26|
27|### 1. Domain / Business Logic (`Logic/`)
28|
29|#### Namespace & File Location
30|```
31|namespace FCM\Logic;                   // top-level logic
32|namespace FCM\Logic\Pricing\Adjustment; // sub-domain
33|```
34|File path must mirror namespace: `Logic/Pricing/Adjustment/DamageFlat.php`
35|
36|#### Class Naming
37|| Suffix | When to use | Example |
38||--------|-------------|---------|
39|| *(none)* | Pure domain objects / Value Objects | `DamageFlat`, `Notification` |
40|| `_Service` | Orchestration + external calls | `Status_Service`, `AIS_pushService` |
41|| `_Logic` | Domain rules without external I/O | `Buy_Back_Logic`, `Address_Logic` |
42|| `Factory` | Object creation with branching | `ProviderRegisterFactory`, `AjaxResponseFactory` |
43|| `*Interface` | Contracts (no `I` prefix) | `Service_Interface`, `PricingAdjustmentInterface` |
44|
45|#### Standard File Header
46|Every PHP file must declare strict types and carry a PHPDoc block:
47|```php
48|<?php declare(strict_types = 1);
49|namespace FCM\Logic\Pricing\Adjustment;
50|
51|/**
52| * Short single-sentence description.
53| *
54| * @package   FCM\Logic\Pricing\Adjustment
55| * @author    Name <email@fcm-eu.com>
56| * @copyright Fleet Control Monitor GmbH
57| * @version   1.0.0
58| * @since     1.0.0 FCM-XXXX Description (INITIALS YYYY-MM-DD)
59| */
60|```
61|
62|#### Typical Logic Class
63|```php
64|<?php declare(strict_types = 1);
65|namespace FCM\Logic\Pricing\Adjustment;
66|
67|use FCM\Traits\ErrorContainer;
68|
69|final class DamageFlat extends AbstractAdjustment
70|{
71|    use ErrorContainer;
72|
73|    public const OPTION_FLAT       = 'flat';
74|    public const OPTION_PERCENTAGE = 'percentage';
75|    public const OPTION_DAMAGE     = 'damage';
76|
77|    public function __construct(array $options)
78|    {
79|        parent::__construct($options);
80|    }
81|
82|    public function getValue(): float { ... }
83|}
84|```
85|
86|#### Do / Don't
87|| ✅ Do | ❌ Don't |
88||-------|---------|
89|| Use `declare(strict_types = 1)` | Omit strict types |
90|| Use `OPTION_*` / `TYPE_*` class constants instead of enums | Use bare strings as magic values |
91|| Use `final` for concrete domain classes | Leave everything non-final |
92|| Use trait `ErrorContainer` for error accumulation | Throw exceptions for validation errors |
93|| Write `@covers` annotations on every test method | Skip `@covers` |
94|| Add `@since` with ticket number | Omit change history |
95|
96|---
97|
98|### 2. Application / Orchestration (`Frontend/`, `AJAX_Scripts/`)
99|
100|#### Namespace & File Location
101|```
102|namespace FCM\Frontend;
103|```
104|File: `Frontend/FleetStockController.php`
105|
106|#### Entry Points
107|| File | Purpose |
108||------|---------|
109|| `fcmRequire.php` | Web requests — bootstraps DB, cache, language, CSRF |
110|| `fcmRequireAjax.php` | AJAX requests |
111|| `fcmRequireCli.php` | CLI scripts |
112|| `fcmRequireCron.php` | Cron jobs |
113|
114|#### Bootstrap sequence (web)
115|```php
116|require_once __DIR__ . '/../DataIntegration/autoload.php';
117|DiLogger::defineLogLevel();
118|DataIntegration::init($profilingOptions);
119|// SSL + Referer + CSRF gate
120|if (DiFunctions::checkSsl(true) && Functions::checkReferer() && Functions::checkCsrf()) {
121|    $database = Database::getInstance();
122|    $mysql    = $database->getMySqliReader();
123|    $trans    = new transakt($database);
124|    $obj_language = language::getInstance();
125|}
126|TokenRequest::runScreen();
127|```
128|
129|#### AJAX Response pattern
130|Always use `AjaxResponseFactory` — never `echo json_encode(...)` directly:
131|```php
132|AjaxResponseFactory::generateResponse(
133|    AjaxResponseFactory::STATUS_CODE_201,
134|    'Saved successfully',
135|    'Success'
136|);
137|AjaxResponseFactory::addEmbedded($messageStack, 'error');
138|AjaxResponseFactory::setResponseCodeAndInformationByStatusCode(201);
139|$response = AjaxResponseFactory::getResponse(); // returns AjaxResponse
140|header($response->getApplicationType());
141|echo $response->toJson();
142|```
143|
144|Content-Type headers:
145|- Success → `Content-Type: application/hal+json`
146|- Error → `Content-Type: application/problem+json`
147|
148|#### Do / Don't
149|| ✅ Do | ❌ Don't |
150||-------|---------|
151|| Include correct `fcmRequire*.php` for the request type | Mix web/CLI bootstrap files |
152|| Use `AjaxResponseFactory` for all JSON responses | `echo json_encode(...)` raw |
153|| Use `TokenRequest::runScreen()` for token auth | Bypass auth checks |
154|| Use `global $mysql, $trans` after bootstrap | Create new DB connections manually |
155|| Validate CSRF via `Functions::checkCsrf()` | Skip CSRF on POST endpoints |
156|
157|---
158|
159|### 3. Infrastructure / Data Access
160|
161|#### Query Object Pattern (`DI\Backend` — preferred; `FCM\Backend` — deprecated)
162|
163|The DB layer uses a **custom Query Object** (not Doctrine/Eloquent). Base class:
164|`/var/www/html/fcm/Tools/Query/query.php` → extended by `FCM_Query` (deprecated) or the `DI`
165|equivalents.
166|
167|```php
168|// FCM\Backend example — READ ONLY, do not extend for new code
169|abstract class FCM_Query extends query
170|{
171|    use Translator, AccessTrait;
172|
173|    protected string $table;
174|    protected string $primary_key;
175|    protected array  $fieldlist;
176|
177|    public function __construct($primaryValue = false)
178|    {
179|        parent::__construct($primaryValue);
180|        $this->table       = 'my_table';
181|        $this->primary_key = 'My_Table_ID';
182|        $this->fieldlist['Column_Name'] = '';
183|    }
184|}
185|```
186|
187|**All new Query classes** → use `DataIntegration` (`DI\Backend`), not `FCM\Backend`.
188|
189|#### Transaction Handling
190|```php
191|$trans = new transakt($database);        // wraps mysqli
192|$trans->beginTransaction();
193|try {
194|    // ... write queries
195|    $trans->commit();
196|} catch (Exception $e) {
197|    $trans->rollBack();
198|    ErrorHandler::logException($e);
199|}
200|```
201|
202|#### Global DB Access
203|After bootstrap, two globals are available everywhere:
204|```php
205|global $mysql;  // mysqli reader (SELECT)
206|global $trans;  // transakt — write operations + transactions
207|```
208|
209|#### Do / Don't
210|| ✅ Do | ❌ Don't |
211||-------|---------|
212|| Use `DI\Backend\*` for all new query classes | Add new classes to `FCM\Backend` |
213|| Wrap writes in transactions | Fire `INSERT`/`UPDATE` outside `$trans` |
214|| Use `ErrorHandler::logException($e)` on DB errors | Silent `catch` blocks |
215|| Use `$trans->rollBack()` on failure | Let failed transactions hang |
216|| Reuse `$mysql` reader for SELECTs | Instantiate a new DB connection |

274|## Error Handling
275|
276|### Exception Strategy
277|
278|| Situation | Pattern |
279||-----------|---------|
280|| User-facing validation failures | `$this->addError(...)` via `ErrorContainer` trait — do **not** throw |
281|| Infrastructure failures (DB, I/O) | Throw `Exception`, catch at bootstrap level |
282|| Top-level catch | `Functions::showErrorPage()` — redirect to `index_error.php` |
283|| Logging | `ErrorHandler::logException(new Exception($msg))` |
284|| Validator errors | Extend `Laminas\Validator\AbstractValidator`, throw `InvalidArgumentException` |
285|
286|### Logging
287|```php
288|use Lib\ErrorHandler;
289|use Lib\DiLogger;
290|
291|// Log exception
292|ErrorHandler::logException(new Exception('Something went wrong', $errorCode));
293|ErrorHandler::invokeHandler();
294|
295|// Set log level (bootstrap)
296|DiLogger::defineLogLevel();
297|```
298|
299|**Rule**: Never catch-and-swallow silently. Either log or rethrow.

303|## Autoloading
304|
305|FCM uses a **custom indexed autoloader** (`autoloader.php`) — no Composer PSR-4.
306|
307|### How it works
308|1. On first load, `autoload_autoloader::init()` scans all registered `$src` directories
309|2. Builds a `className → directory` index, stored in cache (`Lib\Cache`)
310|3. On class load: splits FQCN, takes the short class name, looks it up in the index
311|4. Requires `{directory}/{ClassName}.php`
312|
313|### Registered source directories (partial)
314|```
315|Backend/         Frontend/        Logic/           Traits/
316|Tools/Query/     Tools/CSV/       Tools/FCM_PDF/   Variables/
317|Interfaces/      Imports/         QueryTemplate/   RabbitMQ/
318|Subv/Hertz/      Subv/ALD/        ... (all 48 Subv variants)
319|```
320|
321|### Implications for new files
322|- **A new class is only discoverable if its directory is listed in `$src`.**
323|- New top-level directories **must** be added to `autoloader.php::$src`.
324|- Subdirectories inside already-registered dirs (e.g., `Logic/Pricing/Adjustment/`) are **not**
325|  auto-discovered — they too must be explicitly registered.
326|- **Namespace collisions**: two classes with the same short name in different directories → last
327|  one registered wins. Avoid duplicate short class names across modules.

1|# DataIntegration Copilot Guidelines
2|
3|## Executive summary
4|
5|- Scope used for this document: `DataIntegration/**` excluding `DataIntegration/vendor/**` and `DataIntegration/db/**`.
6|- Autoloading is PSR-style but split by namespace root:
7|  - `DI\` -> `DataIntegration/src`
8|  - `Service\` -> `DataIntegration/Service`
9|  - `UnitTest\` -> `DataIntegration/UnitTest`
10|  - `Lib\` -> `DataIntegration/lib`
11|- This codebase is **layered, but not cleanly isolated**. The biggest legacy quirk is that many “domain” objects are generated database backends in `src/Backend/**` that directly extend `DI\Config\Database`.
12|- There is **no repository layer** in the analyzed paths. Persistence is usually done through:
13|  - generated backend objects (`load()`, `search()`, `expect()`, `save()`)
14|  - raw SQL helpers (`Database::getTableData()`, `Database::updateTable()`)
15|  - shared SQL traits (`src/Traits/Queries.php`)
16|  - stored procedures via `src/Controller/ProcedureController.php`
17|- API/service entrypoints are mixed:
18|  - SOAP-style services live under `Service/*Service.php`
19|  - custom JSON API lives under `Service/API/**`
20|  - outbound integrations live under `Service/REST/**` and `Service/RMQ/**`
21|- For database/schema knowledge, read `src/Backend/**/*.php`. Those generated classes expose table names, primary keys, field constants, defaults, and DB enum metadata.
22|
23|## Architectural boundaries and dependency flow
24|
25|### Practical layer map
26|
27|| Layer | Typical paths | What it does | Depends on |
28||---|---|---|---|
29|| Domain-ish data model | `src/Backend/**`, `src/DataTransfer/**`, `src/Exception/**`, `src/Interfaces/**`, `src/DataAbstraction/**` | Backend models, DTOs, typed constants, business exceptions | `src/Config/Database.php`, traits, `lib/**` |
30|| Application/orchestration | `src/Logic/**`, `src/Controller/**`, `Service/*Service.php`, `Service/Logic/**`, `Service/API/Logic/**` | Validates input, coordinates use cases, calls backends/integrations, builds responses | Domain-ish layer + infrastructure |
31|| Infrastructure/transport | `src/Config/**`, `src/Traits/Queries.php`, `src/Traits/Transaction.php`, `Service/API/Core/**`, `Service/API/Middlewares/**`, `Service/REST/**`, `Service/RMQ/**`, `lib/**` | DB access, transactions, HTTP routing, middleware, REST clients, logging, caching | external libs + globals/config |
32|
33|### Dependency flow
34|
35|Observed dependency direction is usually:
36|
37|`transport/integration -> application logic -> backend models / DB helpers -> lib/config`
38|
39|Examples from the repo:
40|
41|- `Service\ContractService` validates SOAP payloads, loads `DI\Backend\*` objects, calls `DI\Logic\*`, and returns a wrapped response.
42|- `DI\Logic\Address\AddressSearch` orchestrates `ProcedureController`, then maps rows into `DI\DataTransfer\AddressStructure`.
43|- `Service\API\Controllers\DynamicServiceController` maps JSON routes to existing SOAP service classes and methods.
44|
45|### Important boundary quirks
46|
47|- **Domain is not persistence-free** here. `src/Backend/**` classes inherit DB behavior from `DI\Config\Database`.
48|- **Infrastructure leaks upward intentionally**: `ErrorHandler`, `Cache`, `DiLogger`, and DB statics are used directly inside application logic.
49|- **Unknown** whether a stricter architectural policy exists outside the analyzed paths.

53|## Coding standards per layer
54|
55|## Domain layer
56|
57|### What belongs here in this repo
58|
59|- Generated backend classes in `src/Backend/**`
60|- DTO-like classes in `src/DataTransfer/**`
61|- Exception types in `src/Exception/**`
62|- small abstractions/interfaces in `src/Interfaces/**` and `src/DataAbstraction/**`
63|
64|### Naming conventions
65|
66|- Backend classes: singular PascalCase class names, e.g. `DI\Backend\Company`
67|- DB field constants: uppercase snake/camel DB names as constants, e.g. `Company::COMPANY_ID`, `Company::KEY_ACCOUNT_E_MAIL`
68|- DTOs: PascalCase nouns, e.g. `AddressStructure`, `ConnectionDetails`
69|- Interfaces: verb/adjective style, e.g. `Validatable`, `SetStatus`
70|- Traits: noun/adjective helpers, e.g. `Transaction`, `Queries`, `Translator`
71|- Enums: **no native PHP enums found**. Enum-like values come from DB restriction metadata or constant holders like `SortingOrder`
72|
73|### Standards
74|
75|- Prefer backend field constants over string column names when using generated models.
76|- Use explicit setters/getters on backend objects; magic `__get/__set` exists in `Database` but is marked deprecated in comments.
77|- Treat `expect()` as the strict lookup API when “must exist” is part of the use case.
78|- Use DTOs as mutable transport structs; the repo idiom is public nullable properties plus constructor defaults.
79|- Keep business exceptions specific (`EntryNotFoundException`, `ProcessException`, `RequirementException`) instead of returning ambiguous booleans when the caller needs context.
80|
81|### Example: strict backend lookup
82|
83|From `src/Config/Database.php` and its usage pattern:
84|
85|```php
86|try {
87|    $partner = Partner::expect($this->getPartnerId());
88|} catch (EntryNotFoundException $exception) {
89|    return null;
90|}
91|```
92|
93|### Example: DTO style used here
94|
95|From `src/DataTransfer/AddressStructure.php`:
96|
97|```php
98|class AddressStructure extends AbstractDataTransfer
99|{
100|    public ?string $name;
101|    public ?int $addressId;
102|
103|    public function __construct()
104|    {
105|        $this->name = null;
106|        $this->addressId = null;
107|    }
108|}
109|```
110|
111|### Do / Don’t
112|
113|| Do | Don’t |
114||---|---|
115|| Use `Backend::expect()` for mandatory records | Invent repository classes not already used here |
116|| Use backend constants for column names | Scatter raw column strings when a backend constant exists |
117|| Keep DTOs simple and mutable | Add framework-heavy mapping layers |
118|| Throw domain-specific exceptions when absence/invalid state matters | Return `false` where callers need actionable error meaning |

122|## Application layer
123|
124|### What belongs here in this repo
125|
126|- `src/Logic/**`
127|- `src/Controller/**`
128|- `Service/*Service.php`
129|- `Service/Logic/**`
130|- `Service/API/Logic/**`
131|
132|### Common service pattern
133|
134|The recurring orchestration shape is:
135|
136|1. initialize logger/config/message handler
137|2. validate header and payload
138|3. load partner/user/backend objects
139|4. call a logic class or perform backend operations
140|5. convert known business exceptions into response errors
141|6. log unexpected exceptions and return a generic/public-safe error
142|
143|### Standards
144|
145|- Constructors usually call a local `init()` or `parent::__construct('ServiceName')`.
146|- Validate transport payloads before doing side effects:
147|  - SOAP: `Service\Logic\SchemaValidator`
148|  - API: middleware + controller guards
149|- Keep service classes orchestration-heavy and persistence-light.
150|- Prefer composing existing logic/backends over embedding large SQL in service controllers.
151|- Convert expected/user-induced failures into response errors near the boundary.
152|- Bubble unexpected exceptions until the service/controller boundary, then log and normalize the response.
153|
154|### Example: SOAP-style orchestration
155|
156|Based on `Service/ContractService.php`:
157|
158|```php
159|$validationResult = $this->validateSchema(Contract::class, $header, $details);
160|if ($validationResult !== true) {
161|    return $validationResult;
162|}
163|
164|$partner = new Partner();
165|$partner->load($this->messageHandler->getPartnerId());
166|
167|$contractCreation = new ContractCreation();
168|$contractCreation->setPartner($partner);
169|$response->contractId = $contractCreation->create();
170|```
171|
172|### Example: transaction wrapper idiom
173|
174|Observed in `src/Logic/Inspection/Status.php` and `src/Logic/VehicleLogic.php`:
175|
176|```php
177|try {
178|    $this->startTransaction();
179|    $vehicle->save();
180|    $this->commitTransaction();
181|} catch (Exception $exception) {
182|    $this->rollbackTransaction();
183|    ErrorHandler::trigger($exception, E_NOTICE);
184|}
185|```
186|
187|### Do / Don’t
188|
189|| Do | Don’t |
190||---|---|
191|| Validate before calling logic with side effects | Mix request parsing, validation, DB writes, and formatting in one long method |
192|| Catch `EntryNotFoundException` / `ProcessException` at service boundaries when they become user-facing errors | Catch broad `Exception` too early and hide business errors |
193|| Use `MessageHandler` / response wrappers consistently in SOAP services | Return ad-hoc response shapes from similar service methods |
194|| Use `Transaction` trait around multi-write units | Partially persist changes without rollback handling |

198|## Infrastructure layer
199|
200|### What belongs here in this repo
201|
202|- `src/Config/**`
203|- `src/Traits/Queries.php`
204|- `src/Traits/Transaction.php`
205|- `Service/API/Core/**`
206|- `Service/API/Middlewares/**`
207|- `Service/REST/**`
208|- `Service/RMQ/**`
209|- `lib/**`
210|
211|### Database access summary
212|
213|#### Primary patterns actually used
214|
215|1. **Generated backend CRUD**
216|   - `load()` returns object-or-null semantics through `Database`
217|   - `expect()` throws `EntryNotFoundException`
218|   - `search()` returns arrays of backend objects
219|   - `save()` decides insert vs update
220|
221|2. **Raw SQL helpers**
222|   - `Database::getTableData($sql, ...)`
223|   - `Database::updateTable($sql)`
224|   - `Queries::executeQuery()` in shared traits/classes
225|
226|3. **Stored procedures**
227|   - `ProcedureController::callProcedure()` builds a `CALL procedure_controller(...)` statement and returns rows.
228|
229|#### Reader/writer behavior
230|
231|- `DI\Config\Database` switches between reader and writer connections in `checkReaderWriter()`.
232|- Selects normally go to reader.
233|- Writes and explicit transactions force writer.
234|- There is replica-lag mitigation via `avoidReplicationLag()`.
235|
236|#### Transactions
237|
238|- Transaction handling is trait-based: `startTransaction()`, `commitTransaction()`, `rollbackTransaction()`.
239|- It toggles DB autocommit through the singleton `Database` instance.
240|- The trait supports an optional transaction id string; some services use that guard, some do not.
241|
242|#### Error wrapping
243|
244|- Low-level DB failures throw `DI\Exception\DatabaseException` from `Database::execute()`.
245|- Convenience methods often catch exceptions, call `ErrorHandler::trigger(...)`, and return `false`, `[]`, or `null`.
246|- This means caller behavior is mixed: some code relies on exceptions, some on sentinel values.
247|
248|### API I/O conventions
249|
250|#### Custom JSON API (`Service/API/**`)
251|
252|- Entrypoint: `Service/API/api.php`
253|- Router: `Service\API\Core\Router`
254|- Request body: JSON from `php://input`, decoded to array
255|- Route params: extracted from placeholders like `/{service}/{method}`
256|- Response helper: `Service\API\Core\Response::json()`
257|- Normal envelope: `{"status": <httpStatus>, "data": <payload>}`
258|
259|Important quirks:
260|
261|- `Request` stores data in **static properties**, so treat it as request-scoped by convention, not by strong isolation.
262|- `RateLimit` returns raw JSON without the normal `Response::json()` envelope.
263|- `Router` catches `Throwable` and currently returns 404 for thrown route errors, not necessarily the true failure class.
264|
265|#### SOAP-style services (`Service/*Service.php`)
266|
267|- Methods usually accept `stdClass` payloads containing `header` and `payload`/`details`.
268|- Responses are wrapped as `<methodName>Result` objects.
269|- `MessageHandler` is the standard way to create acknowledgements, payload collections, and error blocks.
270|
271|### Example: procedure-based DB access
272|
273|Based on `src/Controller/ProcedureController.php`:
274|
275|```php
276|$this->procedure->setMainlist(ProcedureController::PROCEDURE_ADDRESS);
277|$this->procedure->setList(AddressSearch::LIST);
278|$this->procedure->setWhere(" AND $compare");
279|$result = $this->procedure->callProcedure();
280|```
281|
282|### Example: API middleware contract
283|
284|From `Service/API/Middlewares/Auth.php`:
285|
286|```php
287|public static function handle(Closure $next): mixed
288|{
289|    if (empty(DI_PHP_AUTH_USER) || empty(DI_PHP_AUTH_PW)) {
290|        Response::json(['error' => HttpCodes::UNAUTHORIZED], 401);
291|    }
292|
293|    return $next();
294|}
295|```
296|
297|### Do / Don’t
298|
299|| Do | Don’t |
300||---|---|
301|| Use `Database` helpers/backends the way existing code does | Introduce a second persistence style unless required |
302|| Keep SQL in heredoc strings when following existing query-heavy modules | Mix unreviewed SQL string building and transport code arbitrarily |
303|| Use `Transaction` for multi-write operations | Assume `save()` chains are automatically atomic |
304|| Reuse `Response::json()` / `MessageHandler` for transport consistency | Return inconsistent envelopes for similar endpoints |

308|## Error handling guidelines
309|
310|### Exception types observed
311|
312|- User/business-side exceptions:
313|  - `EntryNotFoundException`
314|  - `ProcessException`
315|  - `RequirementException`
316|  - `DuplicateEntryException`
317|  - `AccessException`
318|- System-side exceptions:
319|  - `DatabaseException`
320|  - broader `Exception` / `Throwable`
321|
322|### Catch vs bubble
323|
324|- **Catch and convert near service/controller boundaries** when the caller needs a user-safe response.
325|  - Example: SOAP services catch `EntryNotFoundException | ProcessException | AccessException` and call `messageHandler->addError(...)`.
326|- **Bubble within core logic** when the caller can decide whether absence or invalid state is exceptional.
327|  - Example idiom: `Backend::expect()` throws instead of silently returning empty.
328|- **Log unexpected exceptions**, then return a generic/public-safe message.
329|  - Common constant: `PUBLIC_EXCEPTION_MESSAGE`
330|
331|### Logging policy actually seen
332|
333|- Global bootstrap installs `Lib\ErrorHandler` from `autoload.php`.
334|- Service/API code also uses `Lib\DiLogger` directly.
335|- API-specific logging goes through `Service\API\Helpers\LogHelper`.
336|- In `UnitTest`, `ErrorHandler::logException()` short-circuits when `DI_INVOKER === 'UnitTest'`.
337|
338|### Legacy risks / quirks
339|
340|- `ErrorHandler` is global and has side effects beyond logging (mailing, redirects, shutdown handling).
341|- Some methods both log and return sentinel values, so failure handling is inconsistent across call sites.
342|- `Service\API\Controllers\WebhooksController::oneAis()` logs caught exceptions but does not emit an explicit error response in that catch block.

421|## Definition of Done for new PRs
422|
423|- [ ] File placement matches existing namespace roots (`src`, `Service`, `UnitTest`, `lib`).

1|# FCM Copilot Guidelines
2|
3|## Executive Summary
4|
5|FCM is a **legacy PHP monolith** (no Composer, no PSR-4 strict autoloading) with a **custom
6|`spl_autoload_register`-based autoloader** (`autoloader.php`). The codebase has no formal
7|DDD layering, but a **de-facto 5-layer separation** has emerged over time:
8|
9|| Layer | Directory | Role |
10||-------|-----------|------|
11|| **Presentation** | `Frontend/`, `Frontend_Template/`, `AJAX_Scripts/` | HTML rendering, AJAX endpoints |
12|| **Business Logic** | `Logic/` | Domain rules, orchestration, services |
13|| **Data Access** | `Backend/` ⚠️ **DEPRECATED** | Query Objects wrapping raw `mysqli` |
14|| **Infrastructure / Tools** | `Tools/`, `RabbitMQ/`, `Consumer/`, `Cron/` | PDF, mail, CSV, message queues |
15|| **Configuration / Tenancy** | `Subv/`, `Variables/` | 48 partner-specific overrides |
16|
17|The **preferred data access path** is through the `DataIntegration` (`DI\*`) layer, not
18|`FCM\Backend`. All new Query classes should live in `DataIntegration`.
19|
20|Dependencies flow: `Frontend → Logic → DI\Backend (DataIntegration)`.  
21|`FCM\Backend\*` is still present for legacy reasons — do **not** add new classes there.
22|
23|---
24|
25|## Coding Standards per Layer
26|
27|### 1. Domain / Business Logic (`Logic/`)
28|
29|#### Namespace & File Location
30|```
31|namespace FCM\Logic;                   // top-level logic
32|namespace FCM\Logic\Pricing\Adjustment; // sub-domain
33|```
34|File path must mirror namespace: `Logic/Pricing/Adjustment/DamageFlat.php`
35|
36|#### Class Naming
37|| Suffix | When to use | Example |
38||--------|-------------|---------|
39|| *(none)* | Pure domain objects / Value Objects | `DamageFlat`, `Notification` |
40|| `_Service` | Orchestration + external calls | `Status_Service`, `AIS_pushService` |
41|| `_Logic` | Domain rules without external I/O | `Buy_Back_Logic`, `Address_Logic` |
42|| `Factory` | Object creation with branching | `ProviderRegisterFactory`, `AjaxResponseFactory` |
43|| `*Interface` | Contracts (no `I` prefix) | `Service_Interface`, `PricingAdjustmentInterface` |
44|
45|#### Standard File Header
46|Every PHP file must declare strict types and carry a PHPDoc block:
47|```php
48|<?php declare(strict_types = 1);
49|namespace FCM\Logic\Pricing\Adjustment;
50|
51|/**
52| * Short single-sentence description.
53| *
54| * @package   FCM\Logic\Pricing\Adjustment
55| * @author    Name <email@fcm-eu.com>
56| * @copyright Fleet Control Monitor GmbH
57| * @version   1.0.0
58| * @since     1.0.0 FCM-XXXX Description (INITIALS YYYY-MM-DD)
59| */
60|```
61|
62|#### Typical Logic Class
63|```php
64|<?php declare(strict_types = 1);
65|namespace FCM\Logic\Pricing\Adjustment;
66|
67|use FCM\Traits\ErrorContainer;
68|
69|final class DamageFlat extends AbstractAdjustment
70|{
71|    use ErrorContainer;
72|
73|    public const OPTION_FLAT       = 'flat';
74|    public const OPTION_PERCENTAGE = 'percentage';
75|    public const OPTION_DAMAGE     = 'damage';
76|
77|    public function __construct(array $options)
78|    {
79|        parent::__construct($options);
80|    }
81|
82|    public function getValue(): float { ... }
83|}
84|```
85|
86|#### Do / Don't
87|| ✅ Do | ❌ Don't |
88||-------|---------|
89|| Use `declare(strict_types = 1)` | Omit strict types |
90|| Use `OPTION_*` / `TYPE_*` class constants instead of enums | Use bare strings as magic values |
91|| Use `final` for concrete domain classes | Leave everything non-final |
92|| Use trait `ErrorContainer` for error accumulation | Throw exceptions for validation errors |
93|| Write `@covers` annotations on every test method | Skip `@covers` |
94|| Add `@since` with ticket number | Omit change history |
95|
96|---
97|
98|### 2. Application / Orchestration (`Frontend/`, `AJAX_Scripts/`)
99|
100|#### Namespace & File Location
101|```
102|namespace FCM\Frontend;
103|```
104|File: `Frontend/FleetStockController.php`
105|
106|#### Entry Points
107|| File | Purpose |
108||------|---------|
109|| `fcmRequire.php` | Web requests — bootstraps DB, cache, language, CSRF |
110|| `fcmRequireAjax.php` | AJAX requests |
111|| `fcmRequireCli.php` | CLI scripts |
112|| `fcmRequireCron.php` | Cron jobs |
113|
114|#### Bootstrap sequence (web)
115|```php
116|require_once __DIR__ . '/../DataIntegration/autoload.php';
117|DiLogger::defineLogLevel();
118|DataIntegration::init($profilingOptions);
119|// SSL + Referer + CSRF gate
120|if (DiFunctions::checkSsl(true) && Functions::checkReferer() && Functions::checkCsrf()) {
121|    $database = Database::getInstance();
122|    $mysql    = $database->getMySqliReader();
123|    $trans    = new transakt($database);
124|    $obj_language = language::getInstance();
125|}
126|TokenRequest::runScreen();
127|```
128|
129|#### AJAX Response pattern
130|Always use `AjaxResponseFactory` — never `echo json_encode(...)` directly:
131|```php
132|AjaxResponseFactory::generateResponse(
133|    AjaxResponseFactory::STATUS_CODE_201,
134|    'Saved successfully',
135|    'Success'
136|);
137|AjaxResponseFactory::addEmbedded($messageStack, 'error');
138|AjaxResponseFactory::setResponseCodeAndInformationByStatusCode(201);
139|$response = AjaxResponseFactory::getResponse(); // returns AjaxResponse
140|header($response->getApplicationType());
141|echo $response->toJson();
142|```
143|
144|Content-Type headers:
145|- Success → `Content-Type: application/hal+json`
146|- Error → `Content-Type: application/problem+json`
147|
148|#### Do / Don't
149|| ✅ Do | ❌ Don't |
150||-------|---------|
151|| Include correct `fcmRequire*.php` for the request type | Mix web/CLI bootstrap files |
152|| Use `AjaxResponseFactory` for all JSON responses | `echo json_encode(...)` raw |
153|| Use `TokenRequest::runScreen()` for token auth | Bypass auth checks |
154|| Use `global $mysql, $trans` after bootstrap | Create new DB connections manually |
155|| Validate CSRF via `Functions::checkCsrf()` | Skip CSRF on POST endpoints |
156|
157|---
158|
159|### 3. Infrastructure / Data Access
160|
161|#### Query Object Pattern (`DI\Backend` — preferred; `FCM\Backend` — deprecated)
162|
163|The DB layer uses a **custom Query Object** (not Doctrine/Eloquent). Base class:
164|`/var/www/html/fcm/Tools/Query/query.php` → extended by `FCM_Query` (deprecated) or the `DI`
165|equivalents.
166|
167|```php
168|// FCM\Backend example — READ ONLY, do not extend for new code
169|abstract class FCM_Query extends query
170|{
171|    use Translator, AccessTrait;
172|
173|    protected string $table;
174|    protected string $primary_key;
175|    protected array  $fieldlist;
176|
177|    public function __construct($primaryValue = false)
178|    {
179|        parent::__construct($primaryValue);
180|        $this->table       = 'my_table';
181|        $this->primary_key = 'My_Table_ID';
182|        $this->fieldlist['Column_Name'] = '';
183|    }
184|}
185|```
186|
187|**All new Query classes** → use `DataIntegration` (`DI\Backend`), not `FCM\Backend`.
188|
189|#### Transaction Handling
190|```php
191|$trans = new transakt($database);        // wraps mysqli
192|$trans->beginTransaction();
193|try {
194|    // ... write queries
195|    $trans->commit();
196|} catch (Exception $e) {
197|    $trans->rollBack();
198|    ErrorHandler::logException($e);
199|}
200|```
201|
202|#### Global DB Access
203|After bootstrap, two globals are available everywhere:
204|```php
205|global $mysql;  // mysqli reader (SELECT)
206|global $trans;  // transakt — write operations + transactions
207|```
208|
209|#### Do / Don't
210|| ✅ Do | ❌ Don't |
211||-------|---------|
212|| Use `DI\Backend\*` for all new query classes | Add new classes to `FCM\Backend` |
213|| Wrap writes in transactions | Fire `INSERT`/`UPDATE` outside `$trans` |
214|| Use `ErrorHandler::logException($e)` on DB errors | Silent `catch` blocks |
215|| Use `$trans->rollBack()` on failure | Let failed transactions hang |
216|| Reuse `$mysql` reader for SELECTs | Instantiate a new DB connection |
217|
218|---
219|
220|## Traits Reference
221|
222|All traits live in `FCM\Traits` (`Traits/`). Compose them via `use` in classes.
223|
224|| Trait | File | Purpose |
225||-------|------|---------|
226|| `ErrorContainer` | `Traits/ErrorContainer.php` | Accumulate + expose validation errors |
227|| `Translator` | `Traits/Translator.php` | Translation helpers (`$this->trans(...)`) |
228|| `AccessTrait` | `Traits/AccessTrait.php` | Role/permission checks |
229|| `FCMQueryAuditTrait` | `Traits/FCMQueryAuditTrait.php` | Audit trail for DB writes |
230|| `NotificationTrait` | `Traits/NotificationTrait.php` | Build `Notification` objects |
231|| `AjaxServiceTrait` | `Traits/AjaxServiceTrait.php` | AJAX response helpers |
232|| `ValidationHelper` | `Traits/ValidationHelper.php` | Input validation helpers |
233|| `JSONObject` | `Traits/JSONObject.php` | JSON encode/decode helpers |
234|
235|Canonical `ErrorContainer` usage:
236|```php
237|use FCM\Traits\ErrorContainer;
238|
239|class MyService
240|{
241|    use ErrorContainer;
242|
243|    public function process(array $data): void
244|    {
245|        if (empty($data['name'])) {
246|            $this->addError('Name is required');
247|        }
248|        if ($this->hasErrors()) {
249|            return; // caller checks hasErrors()
250|        }
251|        // ...
252|    }
253|}
254|```
255|
256|---
257|
258|## Interfaces Reference
259|
260|All interfaces live in `FCM\Interfaces` (`Interfaces/`). No `I` prefix — always `*Interface` suffix.
261|
262|| Interface | Key Contract |
263||-----------|-------------|
264|| `Service_Interface` | `isServiceManager()`, `isOrderServiceManager()` |
265|| `AuditableInterface` | Audit trail contract |
266|| `ContactInterface` | Contact data access |
267|| `PricingAdjustmentInterface` | `getValue(): float` |
268|| `PricingAdjustmentModelInterface` | Pricing model contract |
269|| `ProviderRegisterInterface` | Provider registration |
270|| `AjaxServicesInterface` | AJAX service handler |
271|
272|---
273|
274|## Error Handling
275|
276|### Exception Strategy
277|
278|| Situation | Pattern |
279||-----------|---------|
280|| User-facing validation failures | `$this->addError(...)` via `ErrorContainer` trait — do **not** throw |
281|| Infrastructure failures (DB, I/O) | Throw `Exception`, catch at bootstrap level |
282|| Top-level catch | `Functions::showErrorPage()` — redirect to `index_error.php` |
283|| Logging | `ErrorHandler::logException(new Exception($msg))` |
284|| Validator errors | Extend `Laminas\Validator\AbstractValidator`, throw `InvalidArgumentException` |
285|
286|### Logging
287|```php
288|use Lib\ErrorHandler;
289|use Lib\DiLogger;
290|
291|// Log exception
292|ErrorHandler::logException(new Exception('Something went wrong', $errorCode));
293|ErrorHandler::invokeHandler();
294|
295|// Set log level (bootstrap)
296|DiLogger::defineLogLevel();
297|```
298|
299|**Rule**: Never catch-and-swallow silently. Either log or rethrow.
300|
301|---
302|
303|## Autoloading
304|
305|FCM uses a **custom indexed autoloader** (`autoloader.php`) — no Composer PSR-4.
306|
307|### How it works
308|1. On first load, `autoload_autoloader::init()` scans all registered `$src` directories
309|2. Builds a `className → directory` index, stored in cache (`Lib\Cache`)
310|3. On class load: splits FQCN, takes the short class name, looks it up in the index
311|4. Requires `{directory}/{ClassName}.php`
312|
313|### Registered source directories (partial)
314|```
315|Backend/         Frontend/        Logic/           Traits/
316|Tools/Query/     Tools/CSV/       Tools/FCM_PDF/   Variables/
317|Interfaces/      Imports/         QueryTemplate/   RabbitMQ/
318|Subv/Hertz/      Subv/ALD/        ... (all 48 Subv variants)
319|```
320|
321|### Implications for new files
322|- **A new class is only discoverable if its directory is listed in `$src`.**
323|- New top-level directories **must** be added to `autoloader.php::$src`.
324|- Subdirectories inside already-registered dirs (e.g., `Logic/Pricing/Adjustment/`) are **not**
325|  auto-discovered — they too must be explicitly registered.
326|- **Namespace collisions**: two classes with the same short name in different directories → last
327|  one registered wins. Avoid duplicate short class names across modules.
328|
329|---
330|
331|## Translations
332|
333|Every user-visible string must have a translation entry.
334|
335|### Where
336|`/var/www/html/fcm/DBScripts/scripts/{BRANCH_NAME}.sql`  
337|Check current branch: `git -C /var/www/html/fcm branch --show-current`  
338|If the file doesn't exist, create it.
339|
340|### Format
341|```sql
342|INSERT IGNORE INTO `language` (`Name`, `DE`, `EN`, `FR`, `ES`, `IT`, `NL`, `DK`, `PL`, `SE`, `PT`)
343|       VALUES ('camelCaseKey',
344|       'DE Translation', 'EN Translation', 'FR Translation', 'ES Translation',
345|       'IT Translation', 'NL Translation', 'DK Translation', 'PL Translation',
346|       'SE Translation', 'PT Translation');
347|```
348|
349|### Key naming
350|- camelCase
351|- Descriptive: `vehicleStatusActive`, not `status1`
352|
353|---
354|
355|## Definition of Done (PR Checklist)
356|
357|- [ ] `declare(strict_types = 1)` at top of every new PHP file
358|- [ ] PHPDoc block with `@package`, `@author`, `@copyright`, `@version`, `@since` + ticket ref
359|- [ ] New class directory registered in `autoloader.php::$src` (if new directory)
360|- [ ] No new classes added to `FCM\Backend\*` (deprecated)
361|- [ ] All new query classes in `DataIntegration` (`DI\Backend`)
362|- [ ] Validation errors use `ErrorContainer::addError()` — not exceptions
363|- [ ] DB writes wrapped in `transakt` transaction with rollback + log on failure
364|- [ ] AJAX responses use `AjaxResponseFactory` — no raw `echo json_encode`
365|- [ ] `DataIntegration/UnitTest/{Domain}/{ClassName}Test.php` created with `@covers` annotations
366|- [ ] Tests pass: `cd /var/www/html/DataIntegration && ./vendor/bin/phpunit --colors=never`
367|- [ ] Translation SQL added to `DBScripts/scripts/{BRANCH}.sql` for all new user-visible strings
368|- [ ] `Interface` suffix on new interfaces (no `I` prefix)
369|- [ ] `Trait` suffix on new traits
370|- [ ] Business rules updated in `.dev/fcm/business-rules.md` if domain logic changed
